purpose: Machine-readable Patch 0.7 acceptance. Every Satisfied row must name at least one automated fixture that holds it; every Deferred row must carry the reason it was not built.

rows.statement: Store selection is canonical, and a live store that cannot be opened fails closed rather than falling soft to volatile storage.
Studio never reaches production inventory storage, and never opens the production DataStore even to discard it.
An absent record and a failed read are distinguishable, so an outage cannot be mistaken for a new player.
A write reports committed or failed, and a committed write carries the value the store actually holds.
A read that exhausted its retries blocks writes to that key until a later read reconciles it.
A record over the durable byte budget is refused before submission rather than failing at the platform limit forever after.
A second server can neither load nor mutate a player under a live lease, and its refused write never reaches the durable record.
An acquisition is decided by the committed update, not by a flag left over from a retried transform.
An unparseable lease record is honoured rather than silently overwritten.
A lease holds until its expiry and is takeable at it, so no instant exists where two servers believe they may write.
Shutdown reports which leases it released and which survived, so a partial outage is distinguishable from a clean close.
Leaving releases both the lease and the resident record, so no departed player stays resident or readable.
Exactly one script owns the inventory session lifecycle.
A player whose inventory cannot be leased does not keep playing.
A repeated grant id reads as a replay when the content matches and as a conflict when it does not.
A replayed dismantle is answered from the ledger with the original outcome, across a release and rejoin.
No valuable mutation erases another's replay protection; a destroyed reward stays ungrantable.
Durable ledgers are bounded where the bound can still be reported.
Every durable mutation passes through the canonical owner, and no client-authored value reaches durable state.
Migrations are authored as single-version steps forming an unbroken chain to the current schema.
A migration reports which steps it took.
A record from a newer deploy is refused and preserved, never rewritten at an older schema.
Every supported source schema migrates forward, preserves owned items, and is idempotent on reload.
A migration write-back refuses to clobber a record that changed since the read.
An unparseable record is copied to a derived key and the source is never rewritten.
Every persistence failure reason is classified, and only genuine damage may quarantine.
A record is checkable for duplicate items, missing ledgers, invalid equips, and ownership drift.
Reward, dismantle, and migration writes interrupted mid-flight leave neither durable state nor memory changed, and retry safely.
A crash before the durable commit loses the mutation; a crash after it survives. Both resolve to durable truth on the next load.
A player hopping servers sees the same durable record, and no released server retains it or can still write.
Shutdown accounts for every resident player, cleanly and during a partial storage outage.
Progression and unlocks are a projection of the durable ledger, not a second authority, and a persistence-written ledger is readable by the resolver.
A progression snapshot carries an identity derived from the ledger it was projected from, by content rather than iteration order.
Generated equipment survives persistence, reconnect, equip, and live effect application.
Durable overflow bucket for excess rewards (#54-#57).
rows.note: No durable inventory capacity limit exists; the only capacity concept is the run-scoped survival pack. Building a second durable authority for excess that cannot occur would be speculative.

rows.statement: Separate durable progression/unlock records with their own transaction identity (#64-#65, #67-#68).
rows.note: Progression and unlocks are derived from the grant ledger. A separate record would be a second authority over the same facts, free to diverge - the failure projection.source-binding exists to prevent.

rows.statement: Durable currency contract and atomic currency mutation identity (#66, #69).
rows.note: No durable currency exists. RunCurrencyAmount is run-scoped by name and by use, so there is no qualifying currency and no durable mutation to make atomic.

rows.statement: Configurable latency injection (#84).
rows.note: No persistence path measures elapsed time; every fixture is already free of real waiting, so the injector would have nothing to affect.

rows.statement: Server-only persistence diagnostic snapshot and outcome counters (#86-#87).
rows.note: Nothing reads persistence counters yet. An unread telemetry surface is cost without a consumer; revisit when an operator surface consumes them.

rows.statement: Seedable randomised multi-server stress simulation (#88).
rows.note: The deterministic fault matrix already drives the same paths across servers with named reproducible scenarios; a randomised sweep would trade legibility for coverage already held.
